speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the nature of your chest pain; is it sharp and pleuritic, or does it feel like pressure? Also, how many times have you vomited in the past 24 hours, and does the vomiting bring any relief from the pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture). The history of forceful vomiting (retching) immediately followed by chest pain and choking after alcohol consumption is the classic presentation for a spontaneous esophageal rupture. I will now request a contrast-enhanced CT of the chest to confirm the diagnosis.
